what: the scripted read again saw the $29.99 Team version (3,000 credits) while a browser load of the pricing page showed $49.99 a month for 5,000 credits each, top-ups $10 per 1,000 credits, so the page serves both versions to different loads, as on 10 October; the starting price a browser visitor sees is unchanged, per our 27 October snapshot

the $29.99 Team version and its 3,000-credit tier no longer appear anywhere on the page; Team is $49.99 per user a month for 5,000 credits, top-ups $10 per 1,000 credits (starting price unchanged from 13 Oct), per our 22 October snapshot

the $5, $20 and $50 top-up packs are no longer listed; the page now describes auto top-up of up to $1,000 at a time, and shows yearly totals ($120, $300, $1,200, $3,000) under the $10, $25, $100 and $250 monthly-equivalent prices, per our 22 October snapshot

the page served one Team card on both the scripted read and a browser load: $49.99 a month per user for 5,000 credits, with Free ($50 in credits, 7 days) and Enterprise; the $29.99 for 3,000 credits version seen on 10 October was not served

old: $250 a month, annual billing, self-serve
new: Custom, contact sales

what: Gumloop fixed Pro at $37 for 20,000 credits and added an orchestration fee of 8% on the full list cost of each task (tokens, compute and tool calls), 16% when you bring your own model keys, with overage off by default.
old: Pro slider from $37 (20k credits) to $1,840 (1M credits); unlimited overage by default
new: Pro $37 per month for 20,000 credits; 8% orchestration fee on each task's list cost (16% with your own model keys); overage opt-in, capped at 1M credits

what: Lindy moved from flat per-account plans to per-user plans with a credit pool shared across the workspace, cutting entry Plus to $29.99 per user.
old: Plus $49.99 per month per account
new: Plus $29.99 per user per month (3,000 pooled credits); Pro $99.99; Max $199.99

what: Make collapsed its Core, Pro and Teams tiers into one paid plan with a lower 5,000-credit entry step.
old: Core $9, Pro $16, Teams $29 per month (annual) at a 10,000-credit entry step
new: One paid Make plan from $9 per month (annual) at 5,000 credits

what: Cursor launched an India-only plan priced in rupees and payable by UPI.
old: Cheapest paid individual plan: Pro at $20 per month
new: Cursor Start at INR 649 per month, tax inclusive

what: Salesforce announced a packaged service agent billed only when it resolves an issue on its own, available from July 2026.
old: $2 per conversation or $0.10 per action
new: $2 per resolution

what: Cursor split Teams usage into first-party and third-party pools and added a Premium seat with 5x the Standard seat's usage at 3x the cost, for renewals from July 1, 2026.
old: Standard seat $40 per month
new: Standard seat $40 per month ($32 annual) with more included usage; Premium seat $120 per month ($96 annual)

what: GitHub replaced premium request units with GitHub AI Credits, moving every Copilot plan to usage-based billing at unchanged seat prices (announced 2026-04-27).
old: Premium request allowances; $0.04 per extra premium request
new: Monthly AI Credits included with each plan (1 credit = $0.01); Pro $10, Pro+ $39, Business $19/user, Enterprise $39/user

what: Lovable merged its separate dollar-denominated Cloud and AI balances into the single credit balance used for building.
old: Build credits plus separate dollar balances for Cloud and AI
new: One credit balance for build, chat, Cloud, AI gateway and connectors

what: Zapier moved AI steps, code, MCP and SDK usage into the same task pool, at variable task rates per action, with plan prices unchanged.
old: One task per external-app action; AI steps, code and SDK metered separately
new: One shared task pool with variable per-action task rates

what: Zendesk replaced a single automated-resolution charge with resolution tiers priced by the value the AI agent provided.
old: One automated resolution unit per resolved request
new: Automated resolutions grouped into value tiers; assisted escalations do not count against the allowance

what: HubSpot moved Customer Agent from a per-conversation charge to a per-resolved-conversation charge, paid in HubSpot Credits.
old: $1.00 per conversation
new: $0.50 per resolved conversation (50 HubSpot Credits)

what: HubSpot replaced a recurring monthly charge per enrolled contact with a charge per lead the agent recommends for outreach.
old: Recurring monthly charge for every contact enrolled
new: $1.00 per lead recommended for outreach (100 HubSpot Credits)

what: Windsurf replaced monthly credits with daily and weekly quotas, raised Pro from $15 to $20 and added a $200 Max tier.
old: Pro $15 per month with 500 monthly credits
new: Pro $20 per month with daily and weekly quotas; Teams $40 per seat; Max $200; extra usage at API pricing

what: Intercom changed Fin's billing unit from resolutions to outcomes, which also bill configured Procedure handoffs, at the same $0.99.
old: $0.99 per resolution
new: $0.99 per outcome (resolutions, Procedure handoffs, disqualifications, self-serve routings); $9.99 per sales qualification

what: Gumloop merged its Solo and Team plans into one Pro plan with shared credits and no seat limits.
old: Separate Solo and Team plans with seat limits
new: One Pro plan, shared credits, no seat limits, more credits at the same price

what: Replit cut Core from $25 to $20 a month, added a $100 Pro plan with tiered credits, and retired the Teams plan.
old: Core $25 per month; Teams plan
new: Core $20 per month (includes $20 of credits); Pro from $100 per month

what: Relevance AI split its single credit into Actions (agent work) and Vendor Credits (model costs passed through without markup).
old: One credit covering both agent work and model costs
new: Actions that reset each cycle plus Vendor Credits at cost that roll over

what: Microsoft renamed Copilot Studio messages to Copilot Credits, metered at feature-based rates, with pack price and pay-as-you-go rate unchanged.
old: $200 per 25,000-message pack per month; $0.01 per message pay-as-you-go
new: $200 per 25,000-Copilot-Credit pack per month; $0.01 per credit pay-as-you-go

what: Anthropic added weekly rate limits on top of the five-hour limits for Pro and Max subscribers (announced 2025-07-28).
old: Five-hour rolling limits only
new: Five-hour limits plus an overall weekly limit and an Opus weekly limit; same $20/$100/$200 prices

what: Make switched its billing unit from operations to credits at 1:1, with AI modules priced by actual usage.
old: Billed in operations (one per module run)
new: Billed in credits; most module runs 1 credit, AI features at fixed or token-based rates

what: Cursor moved Teams agent usage to variable request costs and ended unlimited Auto for individuals, counting Auto against included usage from renewals after September 15, 2025.
old: Teams: fixed request costs; Auto unlimited for individuals
new: Teams: variable request costs; Auto draws on included usage at token rates

what: n8n removed active-workflow limits from every plan and moved Enterprise pricing from workflow count to executions, adding a self-hosted Business plan.
old: Plans capped by active workflows; Enterprise priced by workflow count
new: Unlimited workflows, steps and users on every plan; billed by executions

what: the page's plan set changed to $0, $25 and $150 a month, per our July 2025 snapshot; by September 2026 Plus is $16 a month yearly with a per-credit overage
new: $0, $25 and $150 a month

what: Bolt let unused paid-plan tokens roll over for one extra month.
old: Unused monthly tokens expired
new: Unused tokens on paid plans valid for two months

what: GitHub began enforcing monthly premium-request allowances, with extra premium requests billed per request.
old: Premium request allowances announced but not enforced
new: Pro 300, Pro+ 1,500, Business 300, Enterprise 1,000 premium requests a month; extra at $0.04 each

what: Replit switched Agent from a flat per-checkpoint fee to effort-based pricing, one checkpoint per request priced by the work done (new users first, Core and Teams from July 1).
old: $0.25 per checkpoint
new: One checkpoint per request, priced by effort (below or above $0.25)

what: Salesforce made per-user Agentforce add-ons generally available, giving licensed employees unmetered agent use.
old: Consumption only (per conversation or per action)
new: Add-ons from $125 per user per month (unmetered for licensed users); Agentforce 1 Editions from $550 per user per month

what: Cursor moved Pro from a monthly request limit to a dollar pool of model usage at API prices; after backlash it apologised on 2025-07-04 and refunded surprise charges.
old: 500 requests a month for $20
new: $20 of model inference at API prices a month for $20

what: Cursor added a $200 Ultra plan with 20 times Pro usage.
new: $200 per month, 20x Pro usage

what: Salesforce added Flex Credits, billing Agentforce per action instead of per conversation.
old: $2 per conversation
new: $0.10 per action (20 Flex Credits; credits sold at $500 per 100,000)

what: Anthropic added Max plans above the $20 Pro plan.
old: Top individual plan: Pro at $20 per month
new: Max at $100 per month (5x Pro usage) or $200 per month (20x Pro usage)

what: GitHub added a higher individual tier, Copilot Pro+, with 1,500 premium requests a month.
new: $39 per month with 1,500 premium requests

what: Devin 2.0 replaced the $500-a-month team entry price with a $20 Core plan and pay-as-you-go Agent Compute Units.
old: $500 per month (ACUs at $2)
new: Core from $20 (about 9 ACUs), then $2.25 per ACU

what: Windsurf removed flow action credits so only prompts are charged, and cut Teams pricing.
old: Prompt credits plus flow action credits for background tool calls; Teams $35 per user per month
new: Prompt credits only (Pro stays $15); Teams $30 per user per month

what: Manus launched paid credit plans after its invite-only debut.
new: Starter $39 per month (3,900 credits); Pro $199 per month (19,900 credits)

what: Agentforce reached general availability priced per conversation.
new: $2 per conversation, with volume discounts

what: Zendesk introduced outcome-based pricing, charging per automated resolution by an AI agent.
new: Pay per automated resolution ($1.50 committed, $2.00 pay-as-you-go, per eesel)
